preconditions.description: Contract must have non-zero total supply for distributeDividends to succeed

violation_target.exploit_hint: Call distributeDividends(uint256 amount) on either CakeDividendTracker or DogeDividendTracker contract with an arbitrarily large amount. This will inflate magnifiedDividendPerShare and totalDividendsDistributed without any actual tokens being transferred, corrupting the dividend accounting system. The attacker can then potentially claim disproportionate dividends or break the dividend distribution logic for all token holders.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability exists in the DividendPayingToken contract's distributeDividends(uint256 amount) function. This function is PUBLIC and does NOT verify that the specified amount of tokens was actually transferred to the contract. It simply inflates magnifiedDividendPerShare and totalDividendsDistributed based on the provided amount parameter without any actual token transfer. This allows anyone to corrupt the dividend accounting system by calling this function with an arbitrarily large amount.
attempts.attack_strategy: Call distributeDividends(uint256 amount) on either CakeDividendTracker or DogeDividendTracker with a large amount value. This will inflate totalDividendsDistributed without any actual tokens being transferred, demonstrating the vulnerability. The oracle checks if totalDividendsDistributed > initial_value, which will be satisfied after our exploit call.
attempts.step_by_step_plan:
1. Create interface for DividendPayingToken to interact with the tracker contracts
2. Get the CakeDividendTracker and DogeDividendTracker addresses from the main DogeCake contract
3. Record initial totalDividendsDistributed value
4. Call distributeDividends(largeAmount) on one of the trackers
5. Verify totalDividendsDistributed increased from initial value
